title_zh: 黄永玉 · 永远长不大的老头
title_en: Huang Yongyu · The Old Man Who Never Grew Up

lines: 你见过九十多岁还开跑车的老头吗？他叫黄永玉。
Ever met a man in his nineties who still drove a sports car? His name is Huang Yongyu.
可在他心里，他一辈子，都是十二岁那年背着小包袱出门的孩子。
But in his heart, he was always the twelve-year-old who left home with a little bundle on his back.
他的故事，从湘西凤凰开始。
His story begins in Fenghuang, in western Hunan.
沱江的水，吊脚楼，青石板路，他记了一辈子。六十多年后，才全写进一本书里。
The Tuo River, the stilt houses, the stone lanes — he carried them all his life, and sixty years later, he put them into a book.
十二岁，他背着小包袱，顺着小河，穿过洞庭湖，去“翻阅另一本大书”。
At twelve, he shouldered a small bundle, followed the river across Dongting Lake, and set out to read “another great book”.
辗转谋生，没有靠山，只有一支画笔，一把刻刀。
He drifted from place to place with no one to lean on — just a brush and a carving knife.
路上，有位亲人一直牵挂着他，就是表叔沈从文。
Along the way, a relative kept him in mind: his uncle, the writer Shen Congwen.
从一九四六年起，两人书信往来，攒下一两百封信。
From 1946, they wrote to each other — a hundred or two hundred letters in all.
二十九岁，他成了中央美术学院的老师。
At twenty-nine, he became a teacher at the Central Academy of Fine Arts.
可站在讲台上，他心里那个少年，一点儿也没长大。
But standing at the lectern, the boy inside him had not grown up at all.
他画了一只猫头鹰。
He painted an owl.
它曾引来不少风波，后来，却成了他最有名的形象之一。
It stirred up quite a storm — yet it later became one of his best-known images.
一九八〇年，庚申猴年，他设计的生肖邮票发行。
In 1980, the Year of the Monkey, his zodiac stamp was issued.
红底金猴，小小一枚，后来成了无数人珍藏的猴票。
A little golden monkey on red, it became the “Monkey Stamp” cherished by countless people.
八十五岁，他开始在《收获》杂志连载小说《无愁河的浪荡汉子》。
At eighty-five, he began serializing a novel in the magazine Harvest — The Carefree River's Wanderer.
这些家乡的故事，他酿了六十多年，写到得意处，还哈哈大笑。
He had brewed these stories of home for over sixty years, and laughed out loud when a passage pleased him.
二〇二三年六月十三日，黄永玉离世，享年九十九岁。他不愿办任何告别仪式。
On June 13, 2023, Huang Yongyu passed away at ninety-nine. He wanted no farewell ceremony.
可他的猴子，他的猫头鹰，还在对我们眨眼睛。
But his monkey and his owl are still winking at us.
那个背着小包袱的少年，从来没有长大。
The boy with the little bundle never grew up.
